finding: Independent lotteries per item and a waitlist where rejecting loses priority give identical equilibrium outcomes; a common lottery improves match quality; with many low-need agents there is an unavoidable matching vs targeting trade-off

notes: PDF text extracted locally (working-paper version abstract). Supports one common lottery draw per round; participation costs improve targeting.

notes: Applies to public housing queues. Thakral's job-market paper 'The Public-Housing Allocation Problem' not located by title.
